I can’t edit the image here because no image tools are available, but I can give precise, ready-to-run instructions (and example commands/scripts) you can use to change a plain gray background to blue while leaving the person untouched. Work on a copy of the file.

Recommended blue colors (hex): example mid-blue #1E90FF, darker blue #0078D7, or neutral blue #2A6FBA. Pick one or substitute your own.

Photoshop (desktop)
1. Open a copy of the portrait.
2. Duplicate the Background layer (Layer > Duplicate Layer). Work on the duplicate.
3. Sample the background gray with the Eyedropper (I).
4. Select > Color Range. Click the sampled gray in the preview, set Fuzziness to adjust tolerance (start ~20–40) until the preview selects only background. Click OK.
5. With the selection active, choose Select > Select and Mask (or Refine Edge). Set Smooth ~5–10 px, Feather ~1–3 px, Shift Edge slightly inward if needed. Output to Layer Mask.
6. In the Layers panel, create a new layer beneath the masked portrait layer. Fill it with the chosen blue (Edit > Fill or use Paint Bucket with the hex color).
7. If the subject shows a gray color fringe, select the masked portrait layer, Layer > Matting > Defringe (1–2 px) or use Select > Modify > Contract 1 px then mask refine brush to remove halo.
8. Toggle the mask view and paint on the mask with a soft brush (black to hide, white to reveal) to correct small edge errors while keeping the person untouched.
9. Save/export (File > Export > Save for Web or File > Save As). Save a layered .PSD or a flattened .PNG/.JPG as needed.

GIMP (free)
1. Open a copy of the image.
2. Duplicate the layer.
3. Use Select > By Color, click the gray background. Adjust Threshold until selection captures the background only.
4. Select > Feather (1–3 px).
5. Layer > Mask > Add Layer Mask to the portrait layer, choose “Selection” and apply.
6. Create a new layer below the masked layer and fill it with your chosen blue (Bucket Fill with the hex).
7. Use the mask and a soft paintbrush to refine any edge errors; paint black on the mask to hide parts, white to reveal.
8. To remove fringe, right‑click the portrait layer > Alpha to Selection, grow selection by 1 px, invert selection, fill with blue on a new layer, then shrink/feather and blur slightly, or use Filters > Enhance > Heal Selection on edges as needed.
9. Export as PNG/JPEG (File > Export As).

ImageMagick (command-line) — good for truly uniform gray
- First sample the background color (manually or with a tool) or assume approximate gray like rgb(128,128,128). If color varies slightly, use -fuzz.
Example that makes gray transparent then composites blue beneath:
convert input.jpg -fuzz 12% -transparent "rgb(128,128,128)" bg_trans.png
convert -size 1x1 xc:"#1E90FF" blue.png
convert blue.png bg_trans.png -gravity center -compose Over -composite output.png

Or in one line replacing gray with blue (destructive direct replace):
convert input.jpg -fill "#1E90FF" -fuzz 12% -opaque "rgb(128,128,128)" output.jpg

Notes:
- Adjust -fuzz (e.g., 5–20%) to include near-gray pixels without selecting the subject.
- If the person has gray clothing or accessories similar to background, mask selection must be refined manually — automated color replacement may affect them.

Python + OpenCV (script)
- Approach: detect background by sampling border color, build a color-range mask, refine mask with morphological ops and feather, replace background pixels with blue.
Example outline (fill in file names and tweak thresholds):

import cv2
import numpy as np

img = cv2.imread('input.jpg')
h, w = img.shape[:2]

# sample corners or border to get background color median
border = np.vstack([
    img[0:10,0:10].reshape(-1,3),
    img[0:10,w-10:w].reshape(-1,3),
    img[h-10:h,0:10].reshape(-1,3),
    img[h-10:h,w-10:w].reshape(-1,3)
])
bg_color = np.median(border, axis=0).astype(np.uint8)

# create mask by color distance
diff = np.linalg.norm(img.astype(np.int16) - bg_color.astype(np.int16), axis=2)
mask = (diff > 30).astype(np.uint8)  # subject mask: tune threshold

# refine mask
kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (7,7))
mask = cv2.morphologyEx(mask, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel, iterations=2)
mask = cv2.GaussianBlur(mask.astype(np.float32), (21,21), 0)
mask = mask[...,None]

# blue background
blue = np.array([30, 144, 255], dtype=np.uint8)  # BGR for #1E90FF
out = (img * mask + blue * (1 - mask)).astype(np.uint8)

cv2.imwrite('output.png', out)

Notes:
- Tune the threshold and morphological kernel sizes to avoid affecting clothing.
- Use more advanced segmentation (e.g., GrabCut) if person and background colors overlap.

Quick GrabCut improvement (OpenCV)
- Manually provide a rough rectangle around the person and run cv2.grabCut to obtain a clean subject mask, then composite a blue layer behind.

Tips to preserve the person (edge care)
- Work with masks (non-destructive). Don’t use global color replacement unless the background is uniform and distinct.
- Feather/refine mask edges 1–5 px to avoid a hard edge.
- Remove color fringe: contract the mask by 1 px before compositing, or use decontamination/defringe tools available in Photoshop/GIMP.
- Zoom in and manually touch up hair/transparent edges using the mask refine brush.

File handling
- Keep a layered original (.PSD, .XCF) or save an editable version.
- Export a flattened .PNG for best quality (lossless) or .JPG for smaller size (choose quality setting).
